title: Precast T-beam: in-service flexure and construction stage
prompt:
A simply supported precast RC beam, 300 mm wide × 600 mm deep (effective depth d = 540 mm), spans 7.5 m between bearings. Beams are placed at 2.5 m centres and later receive a 100 mm cast-in-situ topping. Concrete C30/37, reinforcement B500B, normal-weight concrete 25 kN/m³.

In service (composite) the beam carries characteristic permanent load g_k = 18 kN/m (including self-weight, topping and finishes) and imposed load q_k = 12 kN/m.

(a) Determine the ULS design moment using EC0 Eq. 6.10. [4]
(b) Design the tension reinforcement for the in-service condition, ignoring any flange contribution, and select bars. Check minimum steel. [8]
(c) During construction the precast beam alone must support its own weight, the wet topping and a construction load of 0.75 kN/m² over the tributary width. Determine the construction-stage design moment and comment on whether the in-service reinforcement is adequate. [6]
(d) State two detailing requirements for the bottom bars at the bearings. [2]
approach: (b) K = M/(b d² f_ck) = 297.4×10⁶/(300 × 540² × 30) = 0.113 < K′ = 0.167 (verify K′ against Singapore NA) → singly reinforced.
A_s = M/(0.87 f_yk z) = 1428 mm² → provide 3H25 (1473 mm²). A_s,min = 0.26 f_ctm/f_yk · b d = 244 mm² (f_ctm = 2.90 N/mm²) — OK. EC2 9.2.1.1.
(c) Beam SW = 0.3 × 0.6 × 25 = 4.5 kN/m; wet topping = 2.5 × 0.1 × 25 = 6.25 kN/m → g_k = 10.75 kN/m; construction q_k = 0.75 × 2.5 = 1.875 kN/m.

w_Ed = 1.35 × 10.75 + 1.5 × 1.875 = 17.3 kN/m → M_Ed = 121.8 kNm; check the precast section (b = 300, d = 540) — the 3H25 is more than adequate, but check props/lifting points and top steel for hogging at lifting.
(d) EC2 9.2.1.4: at least 25% of span steel anchored at supports; anchorage beyond bearing face from l_bd with α factors; consider bearing nib/dowel detailing for precast.

title: Short braced column: axial, then axial + moment
prompt:
A braced short column, 400 mm × 400 mm, is cast in C35/45 concrete with B500 reinforcement. Cover to main bars gives d₂ = 60 mm (d₂/h = 0.15).

(a) The column carries N_Ed = 3800 kN axially. Determine the area of longitudinal reinforcement required, stating the steel stress you adopt and why. [6]
(b) Determine the minimum design moment due to geometric imperfections, EC2 6.1(4). [3]
(c) The column is now also subject to a first-order design moment M_Ed = 120 kNm about one axis. Calculate N/(b h f_ck) and M/(b h² f_ck) and describe how you would use a column design chart to determine A_s. [7]
(d) Check the steel against EC2 9.5.2 limits and specify link size and spacing. [4]
approach: (a) Pure compression: strain limited to ε_c2 = 0.002 → σ_s = E_s ε_c2 = 400 N/mm² (< f_yd = 435). N_Rd = 0.567 f_ck (A_c − A_s) + 400 A_s.
Read the d₂/h = 0.15 symmetric-reinforcement chart → A_s f_yk/(b h f_ck), then A_s,tot. Note chart assumptions (αcc, rectangular block) — verify αcc against Singapore NA.
(d) A_s,min = max(0.10 N_Ed/f_yd, 0.002 A_c) = max(874, 320) mm²; A_s,max = 0.04 A_c = 6400 mm². Links ≥ max(6, φ/4); spacing ≤ min(20φ_min, b, 400 mm) reduced by 0.6 near beams/slabs (9.5.3).

title: Unrestrained platform beam: LTB check and remedies
prompt:
A steel platform beam spans 8.0 m between simple supports that provide torsional and lateral restraint at the ends only. The beam is a UKB 457×191×67 in S355 with: h = 453.4 mm, b = 189.9 mm, t_w = 8.5 mm, t_f = 12.7 mm, r = 10.2 mm, A = 8550 mm², W_pl,y = 1471×10³ mm³, I_z = 1452×10⁴ mm⁴, I_t = 37.1×10⁴ mm⁴, I_w = 0.705×10¹² mm⁶. Section is Class 1 in bending. E = 210 000, G = 81 000 N/mm².

Loading (UDL, applied at the shear centre): g_k = 12 kN/m (incl. self-weight), q_k = 10 kN/m.

(a) Sketch the SFD and BMD with ULS values (EC0 6.10). [4]
(b) Check cross-section bending and shear resistance. [5]
(c) Calculate M_cr (C₁ = 1.127) and the LTB resistance M_b,Rd using EC3 6.3.2.3 for rolled sections. [8]
(d) The beam fails the LTB check. Propose two remedies and quantify one. [3]
approach: (a) w_Ed = 1.35 × 12 + 1.5 × 10 = 31.2 kN/m → V_Ed = 124.8 kN at supports, M_Ed = 31.2 × 8²/8 = 249.6 kNm at midspan (parabolic BMD).
(b) t_f = 12.7 ≤ 16 → f_y = 355. M_c,Rd = W_pl f_y/γ_M0 = 522.2 kNm ≥ 249.6 OK. A_v = A − 2bt_f + (t_w + 2r)t_f = 4094 mm² → V_pl,Rd = A_v f_y/√3 = 839 kN OK; V_Ed < 0.5V_pl,Rd so no M–V interaction.
(c) M_cr = C₁π²EI_z/L² √(I_w/I_z + L²GI_t/(π²EI_z)) = 177.7 kNm.
λ̄_LT = √(W_pl f_y/M_cr) = 1.714; h/b = 2.39 > 2 → curve c, α_LT = 0.49; λ̄_LT,0 = 0.4, β = 0.75 (NA choice — verify Singapore NA).

(d) Remedies: intermediate lateral restraint (bracing/floor connection to compression flange), a heavier/wider section, or a closed/hollow section. With a midspan restraint (L = 4.0 m, conservatively C₁ = 1.0): M_cr = 477.8 kNm, λ̄_LT = 1.045, χ_LT = 0.612, M_b,Rd = 319.5 kNm ≥ 249.6 OK.

title: Pinned column buckling and bolted splice
prompt:
A UKC 254×254×73 in S355 is used as a pin-ended column of system length 5.0 m about both axes. A = 9310 mm², i_y = 110 mm, i_z = 64.6 mm, t_f = 14.2 mm, h/b = 0.98. Section is Class 1 under compression.

(a) Determine the flexural buckling resistance N_b,Rd about both axes and state which governs. [10]
(b) The column is spliced with M20 class 8.8 bolts in single shear, threads in the shear plane (A_s = 245 mm²). Determine the shear resistance per bolt (EC3-1-8 Table 3.4) and the number of bolts if the splice must transfer 25% of N_b,Rd. [6]
(c) Briefly explain how the check changes if the column also carries end moments. [4]
approach: (b) F_v,Rd = α_v f_ub A_s/γ_M2 = 0.6 × 800 × 245/1.25 = 94.1 kN (γ_M2 — verify Singapore NA). 0.25 × 1760 = 440 kN → n = 440/94.1 = 4.7 → 6 bolts (symmetrical). Also check bearing F_b,Rd.
(c) Combined: EC3 6.3.3 Eqs 6.61/6.62 with interaction factors k_yy, k_zy (Annex A or B); check cross-section 6.2.9 and LTB χ_LT for M_y.

title: Strip footing on sand: EC7 DA1 and Schmertmann settlement
prompt:
A 2.0 m wide strip footing is founded at 1.0 m depth in a medium-dense sand (γ = 19 kN/m³, c′ = 0, φ′_k = 32°). The water table is well below the zone of influence. The footing carries a central vertical line load G_k = 250 kN/m and Q_k = 100 kN/m (both including footing self-weight and backfill).

CPT results below founding level: 0–2 m q_c = 6 MPa; 2–4 m q_c = 8 MPa; 4–6 m q_c = 10 MPa; 6–8 m q_c = 12 MPa.

(a) Verify bearing resistance to EC7 Design Approach 1, Combinations 1 and 2, using Annex D. [10]
(b) Estimate the settlement under characteristic (SLS) loads using Schmertmann's method with E = 3.5 q_c (strip), ignoring creep (C₂ = 1). [8]
(c) Comment on which limit state governs the design. [2]
approach: (b) Δp = (250 + 100)/2 − 19 × 1 = 156 kPa; σ′_v0 = 19 kPa; σ′_vp at z = B = 2 m below base (3 m depth) = 57 kPa.
(c) ULS has large reserve; settlement (≈15 mm, acceptable vs typical 25 mm limit) is the more relevant criterion — confirm with structure's tolerance to differential settlement.

title: Cantilever retaining wall: earth pressure and sliding (DA1)
prompt:
A cast-in-situ RC cantilever retaining wall retains 5.0 m of dry granular backfill (γ = 18 kN/m³, c′ = 0, φ′_k = 30°) with a horizontal ground surface carrying a variable surcharge q_k = 10 kPa. The wall base is 3.5 m wide and the total characteristic vertical load on the base (wall + soil over heel) is W_k = 220 kN/m. Base friction δ = φ′ (cast against soil). Ignore passive resistance in front of the toe. Use Rankine pressures on a vertical virtual back.

(a) Calculate the design horizontal thrust for DA1-C1 and DA1-C2. [8]
(b) Verify sliding for both combinations. [6]
(c) If sliding is not satisfied, propose two practical measures. [3]
(d) Sketch the pressure distribution with values. [3]
approach: (b) Sliding R_d = V_d tanδ_d with favourable W at γ_G = 1.0: C1 R_d = 220 tan30° = 127.0 ≥ 126.3 ✓ (marginal); C2 R_d = 220 tan24.79° = 101.6 < 118.6 ✗ FAIL.
(c) Add a shear key below the base (mobilises passive resistance), widen the heel to increase W, or use a sloping base.
(d) Triangular soil pressure 0 → K_aγH (C2 char.: 36.8 kPa at base) plus rectangular K_a q block (4.1 kPa).

title: Expressway incident shockwave and stopping sight distance
prompt:
An expressway lane group follows Greenshields' model with free-flow speed v_f = 100 km/h and jam density k_j = 120 veh/km (per lane).

(a) Determine capacity, critical density and speed at capacity. [3]
(b) Upstream traffic flows at 1800 veh/h/lane (uncongested). A lane-blocking incident causes a queue that discharges at 1200 veh/h/lane in the congested regime. Find the densities of both states and the speed and direction of the resulting shockwave. [8]
(c) Using AASHTO, determine the stopping sight distance for a design speed of 100 km/h (t = 2.5 s, a = 3.4 m/s²) on (i) a level road and (ii) a 3% downgrade. [7]
(d) State one traffic-management measure to reduce secondary crashes at the queue tail. [2]
approach: (a) q_max = v_f k_j/4 = 3000 veh/h; k_c = k_j/2 = 60 veh/km; v_c = v_f/2 = 50 km/h.
(b) k = (k_j/2)[1 ∓ √(1 − 4q/(v_f k_j))]. State A (uncongested, 1800): k_A = 22.1 veh/km. State B (congested, 1200): k_B = 106.5 veh/km.
u_w = (q_B − q_A)/(k_B − k_A) = (1200 − 1800)/(106.5 − 22.1) = −7.1 km/h → backward-forming shockwave moving upstream at 7.1 km/h.
(c)(i) SSD = 0.278Vt + 0.039V²/a = 69.5 + 114.7 = 184.2 m (AASHTO Green Book).
(d) Queue-tail warning via VMS / advance warning signs, variable speed limits, or traffic-incident management to clear quickly.

title: Trapezoidal canal: normal depth, critical depth and profile
prompt:
A long concrete-lined trapezoidal drainage canal has bottom width b = 3.0 m, side slopes 2H:1V, Manning n = 0.015 and bed slope S₀ = 0.0008. Design discharge Q = 12 m³/s.

(a) Determine the normal depth y_n and the mean velocity at normal depth. [7]
(b) Determine the critical depth y_c and the Froude number at normal depth. [6]
(c) Classify the channel slope. A downstream weir raises the water depth to 2.2 m. Name and sketch the resulting water-surface profile. [5]
(d) State one PUB Code of Practice on Surface Water Drainage consideration for such an open drain. [2]
approach: (b) Critical: Q²T/(gA³) = 1 with T = b + 2zy → y_c = 0.947 m. Fr at normal depth = V/√(gD), D = A/T = 0.885 m → Fr = 0.56 (subcritical).
(c) y_n > y_c → mild slope. Weir depth 2.2 m > y_n > y_c → M1 backwater curve, asymptotic to y_n upstream and rising towards the weir.
(d) e.g. freeboard requirement, minimum self-cleansing velocity, maintenance access — check current PUB COP.

title: Primary clarifier and activated sludge sizing
prompt:
A water reclamation plant treats an average flow of 20 000 m³/d.

(a) Size circular primary clarifiers for a surface overflow rate of 40 m³/m²·d and a hydraulic detention time of 2.0 h, using a single tank: determine the area, diameter and side-water depth. [6]
(b) The primary effluent BOD₅ is 180 mg/L. Determine the aeration tank volume for an F/M ratio of 0.30 d⁻¹ with MLVSS = 2500 mg/L, and the hydraulic retention time. [6]
(c) Waste activated sludge is withdrawn from the return line at 150 m³/d with a VSS of 8000 mg/L. Neglecting effluent solids, calculate the solids retention time (SRT). [4]
(d) Explain the effect on effluent quality and sludge settleability of operating at a much lower SRT. [4]
approach: (a) A = Q/OR = 20 000/40 = 500 m² → D = √(4A/π) = 25.2 m; V = Q·t = 20 000 × 2/24 = 1667 m³ → depth = 3.33 m. Check weir loading and peak-flow overflow rate.
(d) Low SRT → higher F/M, dispersed growth / poor flocculation, poorer settleability, little or no nitrification, higher effluent BOD/SS.

title: Reservoir-to-reservoir pipeline in series; upgrade with a parallel pipe
prompt:
Reservoir A (water level 100.0 m) supplies reservoir B (70.0 m) through two pipes in series: pipe 1, 800 m long, 400 mm diameter; pipe 2, 600 m long, 300 mm diameter. Take Darcy f = 0.02 for both. Minor loss coefficients: entrance 0.5 (on v₁), sudden contraction 0.3 (on v₂), exit 1.0 (on v₂).

(a) Determine the discharge. [8]
(b) Determine the hydraulic grade line elevation at the end of pipe 1 and sketch the EGL and HGL. [5]
(c) Pipe 2 is duplicated by an identical parallel 300 mm pipe (each with the same contraction and exit losses). Determine the new discharge. [5]
(d) Why might Hazen–Williams be preferred for a water-supply network check? [2]
approach: Energy A → B: 30 = (v₁²/2g)(0.5 + fL₁/D₁) + (v₂²/2g)(0.3 + fL₂/D₂ + 1.0), with v = Q/A. Coefficients 40.5 and 41.3 → Q = 0.233 m³/s (v₁ = 1.86 m/s, v₂ = 3.30 m/s).
EGL at the end of pipe 1 = 100 − (v₁²/2g)(0.5 + 40) = 92.90 m; HGL = EGL − v₁²/2g = 92.72 m. EGL drops in steps at each minor loss, with steeper slope in pipe 2.
Parallel pipes share the head and each carries Q/2: 30 = (v₁²/2g)(40.5) + ((Q/2A₂)²/2g)(41.3) → Q = 0.357 m³/s (+53 %).
Hazen–Williams is explicit in Q, C tables by material and age (notes p. 106); good for water at normal temperatures, not for other fluids or laminar flow.

title: Broad-crested weir, jump at the toe, V-notch for low flows
prompt:
A broad-crested weir spans a 4.0 m wide rectangular channel. The upstream head over the crest is 0.80 m (approach velocity negligible, free discharge, C_d = 0.88).

(a) Calculate the discharge and the critical depth on the crest. [6]
(b) At the toe of the weir the flow depth is 0.25 m. Show that a hydraulic jump can form, and calculate the sequent depth and the head loss. [8]
(c) For dry-weather flows a 90° V-notch (C_d = 0.59) is installed. Calculate the flow at a head of 0.30 m. [4]
(d) State one condition under which the weir becomes drowned and its rating no longer applies. [2]
approach: Toe: v₁ = q/0.25 = 4.29 m/s, Fr₁ = 2.74 > 1 (supercritical) → y₂ = (y₁/2)(√(1 + 8Fr₁²) − 1) = 0.85 m; ΔE = (y₂ − y₁)³/(4y₁y₂) = 0.26 m.
Drowning when the tailwater rises above about the critical-depth level on the crest (modular limit) — the downstream level then controls.

title: Unit hydrograph convolution, Gumbel design flood, Muskingum coefficients
prompt:
The 3-hour unit hydrograph (1 cm of excess rain) of a catchment has ordinates at 3-hour intervals: 0, 25, 60, 45, 30, 15, 5, 0 m³/s.

(a) Determine the catchment area. [3]
(b) A storm produces 2 cm then 3 cm of excess rainfall in two successive 3-hour periods. Determine the direct-runoff hydrograph and its peak. [7]
(c) Annual maximum floods have mean 420 m³/s and standard deviation 130 m³/s (long record). Estimate the 50-year flood by Gumbel and the risk that it is exceeded at least once in 25 years. [6]
(d) For routing through a downstream reach, K = 12 h and X = 0.2 with Δt = 6 h. Calculate the Muskingum coefficients and check their sum. [4]
approach: DRH_n = Σ P_m U_{n−m+1}: 0, 50, 195, 270, 195, 120, 55, 15, 0 m³/s → peak 270 m³/s at 9 h (add base flow if required).
